idiom_name: value struct + explicit Scan destinations, or sqlx/GORM embedded-struct flattening
implementation_notes: Go has no mapper and no annotation layer in the standard library, so the row-to-value mapping is written by hand: the value is a small struct (no id field) and its fields are passed one by one as Scan destinations, which database/sql requires to be pointers to the individual fields. The idiomatic relief is a flattening helper - sqlx StructScan marshals a row into a struct and supports embedded structs, and GORM's gorm:"embedded" tag with embeddedPrefix flattens a named struct into the parent's columns - but both still require the field-to-column correspondence to be declared, so the classic structure is not absorbed, only automated. Use the hand-written Scan when the query shape differs from the model; use an embedded struct when the same value is read by several queries.
pitfalls: Scan requires a pointer per column: passing the value struct or a non-addressable expression panics or errors at runtime, not at compile time.
A nullable column needs a nullable destination (sql.NullString, *string); scanning NULL into a plain string fails, so the all-NULL-means-absent rule has to be decided explicitly.
Reusing one value struct as an embedded field in two different models silently shares column names - GORM needs embeddedPrefix to keep them apart, sqlx needs distinct column aliases.
